root.label: Study of colorectal cancer in adolescents under 21

events.label: Study of colorectal cancer in adolescents under 21

slots.name: annual case count
slots.sentence: Colorectal cancer in people younger than 20 is exceptionally rare: People like Henderson are about one in a million, and account for fewer than 100 cases per year in the United States.

slots.name: cohort risk ratio
slots.sentence: A person born in the 1990s is four times more likely to be diagnosed with colorectal cancer before age 50 than people born in the 1960s were.

slots.name: study sample size
slots.sentence: The team identified 84 adolescents, with a median age of 16, in the United States who’d been diagnosed with colorectal cancer from 2012 through 2023.

slots.name: advanced stage rate
slots.sentence: It has not yet been published in a peer-reviewed journal.

slots.name: recurrence rate
slots.sentence: Most of the young people in the study, 80%, weren’t diagnosed until their cancer had reached Stage 3 or Stage 4, which means the cancer has spread.

slots.name: pain symptom rate
slots.sentence: In the study, about 74% of people reported back or abdominal pain, and about 45% reported changes in bowel habits.

slots.name: bowel change rate
slots.sentence: and about 45% reported changes in bowel habits.

slots.name: rectal bleeding rate
slots.sentence: A similar portion of people reported unexplained weight loss and about 32% had rectal bleeding.

slots.name: family history rate
slots.sentence: A common risk factor for colorectal cancer is having a first- or second-degree relative — a parent, sibling, grandparent, aunt or uncle — who’d had the disease. But that was only the case for 20% of the people in the study.

slots.name: cancer recurrence rate
slots.sentence: Once a cancer has spread, it’s much more difficult to treat — in the study, about 37% of the patients’ cancer returned and 45% of the patients died.
